2019_138_071619regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of July 16, 2019, at 7:00 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois. The consent agenda combines six sets of June 2019 minutes with the MHSAA membership resolution for August 1, 2019 through July 31, 2020 and the accretion of early childhood educators into the Troy Education Association contract; the personnel item extends administrative contracts through June 30, 2021. The bulkiest new material is a July 15, 2019 memorandum from Assistant Superintendent Rick West weighing renovation of the Niles Center against buying the former ITT Tech building at 1522 East Big Beaver Road, offered at roughly $4 million.

**Personnel (Item 6.A)**
Extension of administrative contracts through June 30, 2021 without tenure in the administrative position and subject to the Administrative Handbook layoff provision, covering principals including Lara Dixon (Athens High School), Remo Roncone (Troy High School) and Joe Duda (Larson Middle School) and directors including Kerry Birmingham, Jessica Carrier, Rob Carson, Tim Fulcher, Erin Keyser, Kandice Moynihan, John Pagel, Christin Silagy and Elizabeth Soggs.

**Other: Niles Center and the former ITT Tech building**
Rick West's July 15, 2019 memorandum prices Niles renovation without demolition at $1,300,000, renovation with demolition at $1,900,000, and full demolition at $500,000, none including flooring or casework. A new building would cost approximately $15-$17 million. The former ITT Tech building at 1522 East Big Beaver Road offers 38,000 square feet on 3.37 acres at $14-$16 per square foot ($532,000-$608,000 per year) or a purchase price near $4 million, plus roughly $2 million to renovate. The aggregate projected June 30, 2020 fund balance of the General, Adult & Community Education, Facility Rental and Capital Maintenance funds is $24,376,142. Attached bond tables model $7,000,000 issues over 10, 15 and 20 years at TICs of 3.00%, 3.25% and 3.50%.

**Meeting**
Troy School District regular Board of Education meeting, July 16, 2019, 7:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Consent items A-H are minutes of the June 4, 2019 Special Board Workshop, June 4 Board Meeting, June 4 Closed Session, June 11 Special Board Meeting, June 11 Board Workshop and June 18 Special Board Meeting, plus the MHSAA Membership Resolution 2019/2020 and accretion of Early Childhood Educators into the Troy Education Association.

**June 4, 2019 workshop and board meeting (Athens High School, 4333 John R)**
President Schmidt opened the workshop at 5:04 p.m. with Superintendent Machesky and administrators West, Harris, Moynihan, Gottlieb, Griffor, Birmingham and Carrier, covering Troy High MEP, vehicle, tractor/loader and robotic arms purchases, the 2018/2019 final budget amendment and proposed 2019/2020 budget, and middle school science materials; adjourned 6:05 p.m. The regular meeting opened at 7:04 p.m. before roughly 300 audience members. Tim Fulcher and the Board recognized the state champion girls' synchronized swim team: Aishwarya Arvind, Katie Austin, Lisa Baek, Hitha Bathala, Sonal Betageri, Sanya Chawla, Fernanda Garcia-Solis, Sarah Godoy, Jillian Hay, Elise Hsiao, Meera Jagan, Nandita Jagan, Vicky Jan, Sonia Kore, Pavithra Krishnan, Nandini Lakshminarayanan, Adia Lee, Camellia Mashal, Grace Neill, Lana Pinjic, Neha Pinnu, Aditi Prabhu, Hannah Richard, Olivia Rosati, Aarushi Shah, Medha Tripathi, Allie Zaluski and Christina Zeng, with All-State Athletes Ana Alvaro, Ashley Bae, Arlene Chen, Elisa DeDonno, Anna Efstate, Kendall Kemp, Shannon Li, Sissie Liang, Sonja Lisowski, Theresa Liu, Sujin Moon, Laura Nicholas, Ellen Olis, Anishka Taneja, Annie Tang, Fiona Warner, Rachel Wu and Aimee Zheng. Academic awards for Boulan Park, Smith, Larson, Baker and Schroeder students spanned the AMC8, Destination Imagination, FIRST Robotics, MATHCOUNTS, chess, forensics, Model United Nations, MSBOA All-State Band and Orchestra, national language exams, Quiz Bowl, Scholastic Art and Writing, the Science and Engineering Fair of Metropolitan Detroit and Science Olympiad. Resolution 19-054 moved the tractor/loader and robotic arms items to Business; 19-055 approved consent items A-E including the April 2019 Treasurer's Report and a transport vehicle purchase; 19-056 awarded the Troy High School mechanical and electrical bid at $205,895.11 from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund (6-1, Hammond); 19-057 awarded robotic arm technology to ABB for $50,519.00 from the 2019-2020 General Fund (6-1, Hammond); 19-058 tabled the tractor/loader. Student representatives were Mackenzie Malinowski, Erin McManus and Jenna Doyle. Resolution 19-059 entered closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) for Superintendent Evaluation, all seven voting Yes; adjournment came at 10:15 p.m.

**June 11, 2019 Special Board Meeting (Services Building, 4420 Livernois)**
Vice President Philippart presided from 5:00 p.m. for President Schmidt, whose voice was hoarse, before about 50 audience members. Julie McClure, President of the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, recognized grant recipients; the Mission Moment honored Larson 8th graders Audrey Brown, Stephen Carlier, Jordan Cruz, Jenna DeJonckheere, Allison Diebol and Gabby Leonard for the Plastic Ocean Project, with teachers Sandy Bammel, Shannon Dziwanowski and Dave Ivanko named TFEE Innovators of the Year. Larson, led by Principal Joe Duda, received the 2019 National School of Character Award from Character.org, one of only 88 schools nationally. Rick West presented the 2019-20 budget book at public hearing; the proposal assumed enrollment of 13,050 students, a decrease from last year. Resolution 19-060 gave Natalie Haezebrouck a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure as Director of Teaching and Learning effective July 1, 2019 (7-0). Resolution 19-061 approved the Bid Pack #23 Resolution Amendment (6-1, Gottlieb) after Gottlieb questioned the 10% contingency and West cited owner's rep Michelle Kerns. Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity and Accountability, reported on science materials assembled by Kate Rainey; 19-062 approved grades 6-8 materials at $507,182.50 (7-0). Resolution 19-063 amended 2018-19 appropriations: General Fund $155,576,715; Food Service $4,334,204; Adult Ed & Community Svc $3,816,201; Preschool $381,705; Facilities Rental $748,176; Capital Maintenance $190,000; 2014 Capital Projects $107,185; 2016 Capital Projects $15,320,000; 2019 Capital Projects $130,062; EC Learning Ctr Capital Projects $13,000,000; Sinking Fund Capital Projects $3,882,000; Debt Service $15,399,958 (7-0). Resolution 19-064 set 2019-20 appropriations - General Fund $158,261,349; Food Service $3,455,345; Troy Career Center $2,445,150; Adult Ed & Community Svc $3,052,976; Preschool $1,996,615; Facilities Rental $161,780; Troy School & Student Activities $5,000,000; Capital Maintenance $500,000; 2016 Capital Projects $8,582,462; 2019 Capital Projects $5,000,000; EC Learning Ctr Capital Projects $5,232,000; Sinking Fund Capital Projects $3,828,500; Debt Service $17,740,610 - with millages of 18.0000 mills non-homestead general operating, 10.8836 mills commercial personal property, 4.8836 mills homestead general operating, 4.1000 mills debt retirement and 0.9857 mills sinking fund (7-0). Also adopted, all 7-0: 19-065, a TelNet Worldwide telecommunications contract for 2019/2020, 2020/2021 and 2021/2022 after Technology Director Beth Soggs cited poor service quality; 19-066, monitors and hardware for secondary computer labs at $103,619.00 from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund; 19-067, iPads from Apple Computers at $367,500.00 and cases from Rug-Ed at $23,232.00; 19-068, Presidio laptops and desktops for the Preschool at $39,823.00; 19-069, renewal with First Student for transportation; and 19-070, a tractor/loader from Rochester Lawn Equipment at $30,969.12. Philippart reported the Superintendent was rated highly effective; adjourned 6:57 p.m. The June 11 workshop ran 7:07 p.m. to 8:45 p.m. on Technology Bond Purchases. At the June 18 special meeting (8:00 a.m.), with Hammond and Schmidt by teleconference and Gottlieb absent, Resolution 19-071 approved iPads and cases from Apple Computers for the High School 1:1 Program at $367,500.00 from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund (6-0); adjourned 8:06 a.m.

**MHSAA membership**
The resolution enrolls six secondary schools, City of Troy, County of Oakland, from August 1, 2019 through July 31, 2020. Executive Director Mark Uyl's May 2019 letter cites Michigan Attorney General Opinion #4795 of 1977 and warns that resolutions not returned by the fourth Friday after Labor Day (September 27) bar post-season entry. Accident medical insurance, provided since 1970-71 for grades 6-12, pays up to $1,000,000 after a $25,000 deductible per claim, with up to $50,000 for paralysis or coma and a $10,000 death or dismemberment benefit (administrator Bryan Cronen, First Agency, Inc.); concussion care insurance, since 2015-16, is limited to $25,000 per accident (administrator Terri Bruner, K & K Insurance Group). Representative Council minutes from Gaylord, May 5-6, 2019 report 750 high schools and 810 junior high/middle schools as of April 1, 2019 against 751 and 752 a year earlier; actions raised the amateur awards limit from $25 to $40, capped 8-player football at 215 students, and approved a 2019-20 budget adding $258,895 in cash with football Final tickets at $15, wrestling Finals sessions at $18 and boys basketball tickets at $12.

**Early childhood educator accretion**
A June 7, 2019 tentative agreement between the district and the Troy Education Association, MEA/NEA adds Article 36, Troy Early Childhood Educators, to the 2017-2020 contract for staff outside the Michigan Teachers' Tenure Act and under Michigan's Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA). Terms include a 24-month probationary period, four-week layoff notice with two-year recall rights, an eight-hour maximum workday, 300 minutes weekly preparation time, mentoring stipends of $500 per mentee with at most two mentees, 30 hours of annual professional development for certificated educators and 24 without a certificate, a $3,000 cafeteria plan in lieu of medical insurance under PA 152 of 2011, $50,000 term life insurance, and long-term disability after 60 days at up to two-thirds of salary to a maximum of $3,000 per month. The salary schedule is Step 1 $28,008, Step 2 $29,564, Step 3 $31,120, Step 4 $32,676 and Step 5 $34,232, effective through January 31, 2021, with a $1,000 annual master's stipend and $24.12 hourly extra-duty pay authorized by the Director of Early Childhood Programs; the 2019/2020 calendar is 192 days inclusive of six paid holidays. Attachments include tuition preschool calendar revisions and a Child Care Supervisor evaluation form.

**Personnel (Item 6.A)**
Administrative contracts are recommended for extension through June 30, 2021 without tenure and subject to the Administrative Handbook layoff provision: Ryan Brinks, Lara Dixon (Athens High School), Remo Roncone (Troy High School), Jonathan Cross, Joe Duda, Anthony Morse, Christian Mueller, Michelle Barsh, Joyce Brasington, Brian Canfield, Mike Cottone, Erin Detmer, Tammy DiPonio, Sarah Glasser, Matt Jansen, Melanie Morey, Shari Pawlus, Jeremey Whan, Stephanie Zendler, assistant principals Melissa Curth, Robert Dowd, Dan House, Brian Zawislak, Cassandra Conaton, Kristy Pierce, David Recker and Kimberly Vergauwen, and Kerry Birmingham, Jessica Carrier, Rob Carson, Christine Foren, Tim Fulcher, Erin Keyser, Kandice Moynihan, John Pagel, Christin Silagy, Elizabeth Soggs and Sarah Young.

**Other: Niles Center invest-or-divest analysis**
Rick West's July 15, 2019 memorandum to Dr. Rich Machesky quotes the Friday, June 28th Communique and estimates $1,300,000 to renovate Niles without demolition, $1,900,000 to renovate after removing the early childhood wing and adding 30 parking spaces, and $500,000 to demolish the building entirely; none include flooring or casework. A Barton Malow partial-demolition estimate totals $1,919,300: $342,900 sitework plus $713,050 of asbestos/architectural/engineering bids ($1,055,950 site), $428,350 architectural, $365,000 mechanical and $70,000 electrical. Niles houses Troy College & Career High School (100 students, 8 to 9 classrooms), Troy Intersect (90 students), Adult & Continuing Education (550 students, five classrooms plus three rented at Walsh College and free space at the University Center in Auburn Hills), Community Enrichment and Athletics. A new building would cost approximately $15-$17 million. The former ITT Technical building at 1522 East Big Beaver Rd is single-story, approximately 38,000 square feet on 3.37 acres, built 1979 and renovated 2011, zoned IB Integrated Industrial Business District, with about 250 parking spaces. Jones Lang LaSalle brokers Robert Mihelich and Jennifer Lech quote $14.00-$16.00 PSF, or $532,000-$608,000 annually, against a sale price near $4 million; JLL's broker opinion of value cites an average comparable of $105.36 per square foot and market values of $3,420,000 low, $3,990,000 mid and $4,750,000 high. TMP Architecture, Inc. estimates $552,000 site cost (repaving $500,000, security lighting $50,000, monument sign $2,000), $40,000 envelope, $500,000 interior classroom enclosure allowance, $50,000 interior LED lighting and $30,000 public address, for a total estimated cost of $1,172,000; the memorandum puts renovation at approximately $2 million. Financing options are Series III Bonds for demolition, the Sinking Fund for real estate, restricted fund balances, General Fund Obligation Bonds and variable rate bonds; usable balances are limited to the General, Adult & Community Education, Facility Rental and Capital Maintenance funds, whose aggregate projected June 30, 2020 balance is $24,376,142. Three tables model $7,000,000 of 2019 School Building and Site Bonds (General Obligation - Limited Tax), County of Oakland, dated Nov 1, 19, first payment May 1, 20, Debt/TV 3.75%: 10 years at 3.00% TIC, average life 6.24, debt service $8,311,000; 15 years at 3.25% TIC, average life 9.09, debt service $9,067,975; and 20 years at 3.50% TIC, average life 12.14, debt service $9,973,600. Each shows existing LT debt of $7,125,000 totaling $10,183,558 alongside $139,575,000 of existing UT debt.
